elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1 retains "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed" and "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." No unlimited-Customer-liability language remains.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 21.1 as rendered: "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." Basis is "fees paid or payable" (not broader "all amounts"), the lookback runs to the claim, and the USD 1,000,000 floor is present. The lower-case "fees" plus the express scope "under this Agreement and all Order Forms" displaces the narrow 1.5 "Fees" (Implementation Fee only) that made the original cap illusory.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.2 (unchanged): "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill" — bilateral on its face.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations", and both 21.1 and 21.2 open "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations" is within Excluded Claims, which sit outside the 21.1 cap.
21.3: "its indemnification obligations" is an Excluded Claim; 21.1 caps apply "Except for Excluded Claims", so indemnities sit outside the cap with no sub-cap retained.
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.
21.3: "... or fraud" is within the Excluded Claims definition excepted from 21.1 and 21.2.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" is an Excluded Claim.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 21.3 as rendered: "Customer's payment obligations, including its obligation to pay undisputed amounts due for conforming Services, are not damages and are not limited by this Section." The carve-out is now keyed to payment obligations generally rather than the narrow defined "Fees" (Implementation Fee), so it covers Customer's payment obligations as a whole.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... The cap is mutual".

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 21.1 limb (a) is "fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve months preceding the claim", with a USD 1,000,000 floor; the basis is no longer the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee.
21.3 Excluded Claims includes "its indemnification obligations"; 21.1 excepts Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations".

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all eleven preferred elements are met in the rendered operative text; the fallback checklist is met a fortiori.

The finding is correctly classified as a deviation before redline: "Fees" at 1.5 is the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee and the cap was keyed to that amount under the first Order Form only, which is far below six months' fees and therefore walk-away territory rather than a minor sub-element gap.

Minimality holds. Only two operative strings changed — the cap basis in 21.1 and the payment carve-out noun in 21.3 — each required by a selected element. Favourable existing language survives (mutuality sentence, the 21.2 direct-damages characterisation of restoration/notification/incident-response costs, "undisputed" and "for conforming Services"). No survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or procedural boilerplate was added.

The temporal anchor was changed from "the event giving rise to the claim" to "the claim"; this sits inside the cap element being rewritten and tracks the element wording literally, so it is not a minimality or intent defect, though the model language's "event giving rise to the claim" formulation was marginally broader and could be restored without cost if the counterparty pushes back.

Preserves intent: no undefined term, dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence. Definition 1.5 is left untouched and still operates for the payment/invoicing provisions; the cap and carve-out now use lower-case "fees"/"payment obligations" with express scope ("under this Agreement and all Order Forms"), so the narrow definition does not bleed back into Section 21.

Residual drafting hygiene point only (not an element failure): because 1.5 still defines "Fees" narrowly, the drafter may wish to say "all fees and charges payable under this Agreement and all Order Forms (whether or not within the defined term 'Fees')" to foreclose any argument that lower-case "fees" imports the 1.5 definition; the USD 1,000,000 floor makes the cap meaningful on either reading.
